newsitem.title: INDIA: India communists threaten coalition over insurance.
newsitem.headline: India communists threaten coalition over insurance.

text.p: The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) has threatened to quit Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition if it pursues efforts to privatise the insurance industry, the Economic Times said on Saturday.
The centre-left United Front government said last year that it would set up an independent Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) to bring in private capital to the state insurance monopoly.

"If the government wants to rule without 33 members of parliament, fine. Then it can try to enact the IRA legislation to open up the sector despite our protests," CPI-M spokesman Prakash Karat was quoted as saying.
A party spokesman was unavailable for comment.
The CPM-Ms a member of the coalition but has no ministerial posts. Its strength is not enough to topple Deve Gowda on its own.

The 13-party United Front, which commands the support of 190 lawmakers including members of the CPI-M in the 545-member parliament, relies mainly on the Congress party, which controls 140 votes, for a majority.

But the CPM-M played a crucial role in setting up the coalition last year when it helped rally regional and leftist parties to join and keep the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from power.
